Consult Summary:
- One-line: Female patient with several days of nausea and dull lower abdominal ache along with feeling hot/sweaty and increased urinary frequency; plan to rule out pregnancy and pursue in-person evaluation and tests today.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Nausea with dull lower abdominal ache; feeling hot and sweaty for about 2–3 days.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began ~2 days ago and have been ongoing; previously described constipation ~1 week ago (resolved); last bowel movement yesterday.
- Associated symptoms: No vomiting, no diarrhea. Urinary frequency without pain or urgency; no foul-smelling urine; no vaginal discharge reported.
- Menstrual/gynecologic: Last menstrual period ~3 weeks ago; intermittent spotting over the past few days; pink-tinged urine noted by patient; due on soon.
- Contraception/sexual: Sexually active with one regular partner; uses Implanon implant.
- Pregnancy: Patient uncertain about pregnancy; doctor advised ruling out pregnancy.
- Past medical history/medications/allergies: Allergic to Amoxicillin; no other chronic medical problems mentioned; on Implanon implant; no other medications reported.
- Social history: Lives with boyfriend; non-smoker; no other social history details provided.
- Family history: Brother with type 1 diabetes.

Examination:
- No physical examination or vital signs documented in the transcript.

Impression:
- Working differential includes simple constipation; other potential causes of lower abdominal ache and nausea/pain; pregnancy should be excluded with testing and further evaluation.

Plan:
- Arrange in-person GP visit today for full examination and investigations.
- Specifically perform pregnancy testing to definitively exclude pregnancy; consider additional examinations or tests as indicated.
- Advise patient to seek urgent care if symptoms worsen (e.g., light-headedness, new concerning symptoms).
- Follow-up to be arranged based on test results and exam.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements: Vital signs and explicit physical examination findings not documented; no pregnancy test results yet; no imaging or lab results provided; no explicit med reconciliation beyond listing allergies and implant.
- Internal conflicts: No clear conflicts detected in the transcript.
- Transcript quality: Some pauses and incomplete phrases; overall enough to plan initial evaluation, but lacks objective data (vital signs, exam findings, test results).
